 PRIVACY News RAF fighter jet declares emergency over Manchester area minutes after take-off
 A Royal Air Force Eurofighter 2000 has declared an emergency near the city at 9,975ft just minutes after take-off, according to flight tracking data
 Share by Annette Belcher, Zahra Khaliq 
 20:34, 27 Oct 2026 Updated 22:42, 27 Oct 2026 
 See news near you 
 A Royal Air Force Eurofighter 2000 has declared an emergency near the city at 9,975ft just minutes after take-off, according to flight tracking data (file pic) (Image: Nicolas Economou/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

You can unsubscribe at any time. More info Thank you for subscribing An RAF Typhoon fighter jet was forced to broadcast an emergency alert whilst above an area near Manchester, aviation tracking figures have revealed.
 The Eurofighter 2000, designated with the callsign COBRA012, beamed a 7700 general emergency transponder signal at an altitude of 9,975 feet at 6:52 pm. The alert was initiated just five minutes into the flight.
 Details surrounding the reason for the emergency signal remain unconfirmed. The RAF said the general emergency was not escalated to its operations team so "was most likely a precaution," The Mirror reports.
 READ MORE:  {{title}} 
 Flight tracking maps show the COBRA 012 transmitted the emergency squawk code 7700 by 6:52pm, when the aircraft was recorded at an altitude of 9,975ft. 
 The Eurofighter Typhoon is a multi-role combat aircraft used by the Royal Air Force for air defence, interception and combat operations.
 The aircraft plays a key role in protecting UK airspace, with Typhoons kept on standby around the clock as parts of RAF's Quick Reaction Alert (QRA) system.
 Show more 
 Jets can be scrambled at short notice to investigate unidentified aircraft or respond to potential threats to British airspace.
 The RAF's two main UK Typhoon bases are RAF Coningsby in Lincolnshire and RAF Lossiemouth in Scotland.
 Both stations operate Quick Reaction Alert aircraft, which can be launched within minutes if required.
